candidates.title: On the interplay between the anisotropy and the regularity of the coefficients in non autonomous problems
candidates.abstract: We establish the local Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers of non autonomous integral {functionals} of the form \begin{equation*} \label{functional} {\mathcal{F}(z) =} \int_ΩF(x, Dz)\,dx, \end{equation*} where $Ω$ is a bounded open set of $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \ge 2$ and the energy density $F(x,ξ)$ satisfies general growth conditions with respect to the gradient variable. The main novelty of this work lies in the identification of a suitable condition on the interplay between the regularity of the partial map $x\to {F(x,ξ)}$ and the ratio of the non uniform ellipticity of the problem that is sufficient to obtain the Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers. Our result extends and unifies those previously known from the literature, including the standard $p-$growth case.

candidates.title: Hankel determinants of Motzkin path generating functions and the Hirota-Miwa equation
candidates.comment: 40 pages; ancillary files contain the computer checks

T. Yu proved Cigler's conjecture $D_{k,n}D_{k,n-2k-2}-x^2D_{k,n-1}D_{k,n-2k-1}=(1-x^2)D_{k,n-k-1}^2$ $(n\ge2k+2)$ by writing $D_{k,n}$ as a $k\times k$ determinant of Chebyshev polynomials modulo $U_k-xU_{k-1}$. Using a linear map found by Yu, we show that the recurrence is a reduction of the Hirota-Miwa equation for Casorati determinants. This gives a second proof, and the recurrence holds for $n\ge2k+2+\max(0,N-\lfloor k/2\rfloor)$ for the Hankel determinants of $n\mapsto L(X^n(U_k-xU_{k-1}))$ whenever the moment functional $L$ has the recurrence coefficients of the Chebyshev polynomials above height $N$. For any monic polynomial in place of $U_k-xU_{k-1}$ the Hirota-Miwa equation gives an identity with a free parameter between symplectic characters, and Yu's identity for rectangular characters follows from it by fixing the parameter and restricting to a line. candidates.title: A proof of Cigler's quadratic recurrence for Hankel determinants of Motzkin path generating functions
candidates.comment: 19 pages; an earlier version is on Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24369438
candidates.abstract: For an integer $k\ge0$ let $a_{n,k}(x,c)$ be the generating polynomial of the Motzkin paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,k)$ that never go below height $0$, where level steps have weight $c+x$ at height $0$ and weight $c$ at positive height, and let $D_{k,n}(x,c)=\det(a_{i+j,k}(x,c))_{0\le i,j\le n-1}$. We prove that for all $k\ge0$ and $n\ge2k+2$ $$D_{k,n}D_{k,n-2k-2}-x^2D_{k,n-1}D_{k,n-2k-1}=(1-x^2)D_{k,n-k-1}^2,$$ a quadratic recurrence conjectured by J. Cigler in 2023 (eq. (18) of arXiv:2309.15557 and MathOverflow question 456683). As a by-product we obtain an expression of $D_{k,n}$ as a $k\times k$ determinant built from Chebyshev polynomials reduced modulo $U_k-xU_{k-1}$, together with a bilinear identity for these $k\times k$ determinants that holds for all integer shifts. We also give a proof of Cigler's companion conjecture that $D_{k,n}(x,c)$ equals the determinant of an explicit matrix $H_{k,n}(x)$ with entries $0$, $1$ and powers of $x$, and in particular does not depend on $c$; this statement has recently been proved by V. candidates.title: Equivariant extension of $I_N$-finite tempered distributions on real flag varieties
candidates.abstract: Let $G$ be a real linear reductive group and let $P=L_PU_P$ and $Q=LN$ be parabolic subgroups. For a Casselman--Wallach representation $F$ of $L_P$, let $\mathcal{E}_F$ be the unnormalized homogeneous tempered bundle on $G/P$ induced from $F$. We prove that every $I_N$-finite tempered distribution on a $Q$-stable Nash open subset of $G/P$ extends to an $I_N$-finite tempered distribution on $G/P$.

candidates.title: Planar cut-and-project sets with interval windows are bi-Lipschitz equivalent to lattices
candidates.abstract: We prove that every cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose window is a line segment is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice: if $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$ is a plane which is not spanned by vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^3$, $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$, and $σ$ is a segment of any length which is transverse to $V$, then the set of points $v\in V$ with $v+x\inσ+\mathbb{Z}^3$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to $\mathbb{Z}^2$. For planes of Diophantine slope this is a theorem of Burago and Kleiner, and the point of the present paper is that no Diophantine condition on the plane is needed. We also show that the same conclusion holds when the window is a finite union of intervals. Together with the author's construction of a cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window of countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to any lattice, this shows that for planes in $\mathbb{R}^3$ the answer to the bi-Lipschitz question depends on the shape of the window rather than on the Diophantine properties of the plane.

candidates.title: Uniqueness of $L_{p}$ Minkowski Problem in the supercritical range near the affine exponent
candidates.abstract: We study the isotropic $ L_{p} $-Minkowski problem. The equation is affine invariant at the exponent $ p = -n-1 $, where all origin-centered ellipsoids with the volume of the unit ball are solutions, and it is known that the unit sphere is the only solution for $ p \in (-n-1, 1) $. We prove uniform $ C^{0} $ estimates for all solutions in the supercritical range $ p < -n-1 $. This allows us to prove a key spectral estimate of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator on solutions. We then utilize the Rayleigh quotient method with position vectors as test functions for the operator adapted from Ivaki-Milman to prove uniqueness in the range $ p \in (-n-1- δ_{n}, -n-1) $ for some $ δ_{n} > 0 $.

candidates.title: Source Conditions and Sharp Transition Asymptotics for the Factorization Method with Far-Field Data
candidates.abstract: The factorization method characterizes an obstacle through a range test, but practical implementations replace the associated Picard series by a regularized approximation. This paper studies the resulting regularization bias for inverse acoustic scattering by impedance obstacles. For a disc, we show that every positive-order Hölder source condition fails at each noncentral interior sampling point, whereas logarithmic source conditions hold uniformly on compact interior subsets for every exponent, with explicit constants. At the center, the bias decays linearly with the regularization parameter. We then derive sharp spectral transition asymptotics through the Lambert W function. These asymptotics determine the stabilization rate inside the obstacle, the iterated-logarithmic growth at the boundary, and the divergence outside. They also yield a threshold rule for which the reconstructed disc converges in measure, together with quantitative boundary-location estimates. For general impedance obstacles, we reduce the spectral decay of the symmetrized far-field operator to that of the data-to-pattern operator and obtain two-sided transition bounds in terms of the inradius and any radius l

candidates.title: The weighted fundamental lemma for non-split groups
candidates.abstract: In this work, we prove the Weighted Fundamental Lemma for Lie algebras for general (quasi-split) unramified $G$. The strategy is to adapt the proof of Chaudouard--Laumon from the split case. In particular, we define the notion of a $ξ$-stable Higgs bundle for a quasi-split reductive group scheme $G$ on a curve, and prove that the stack of such form a proper, finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack over the Hitchin base when $G$ has anisotropic center. We then adapt the global cohomological theorem of Chaudouard--Laumon to the quasi-split setting, and perform the required Frobenius-point count to obtain an identity of adelic orbital integrals. A local-to-global argument deduces the WFL for Lie algebras. In the last chapter, we perform a parallel reduction to deduce Waldspurger's nonstandard WFL from a global version which follows from the same geometric theory. Our work implies the Twisted Weighted Fundamental Lemma in good characteristic, which completes Moeglin--Waldspurger's stabilization of the twisted Arthur--Selberg trace formula. We therefore render unconditional the endoscopic classification for classical groups and an array of downstream consequences in automorphic theory.

candidates.title: The Ritt problem is decidable
candidates.abstract: We give an affirmative solution to the Ritt problem.

candidates.title: Representations of spectral systems over finite distributive lattices
candidates.abstract: A representation theorem is proved for spectral systems indexed by the lattice of down-sets of a finite poset P. Over an arbitrary associative ring, every excisive, homotopy-exact chain system of differential modules is isomorphic to the chain system of a projective P-graded differential module with a single upper-triangular differential. Consequently, every Cartan-Eilenberg system that is excisive and chain generated, together with its spectral system, admits such a differential model. An example over Z/4 shows that chain generation cannot be dropped. A chain system over Z/8 with short exact rows, whose maps commute only up to homotopy, shows that homotopy-exactness cannot be weakened to distinguished triangles in the derived category. Under finiteness conditions the model is finitely generated. The proof combines a derived horseshoe lemma with induction over the lattice, and yields a short proof and extension of Franzosa's connection matrix theory.

candidates.title: Non autonomous problems with nearly linear growth and Orlicz-Sobolev coefficients
candidates.abstract: We establish the local Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers of non autonomous integral functionals of the form \[ \mathcal{F}(u, Ω) = \int_ΩF(x, Du)\, {\mathrm d}x, \] where $Ω$ is a bounded open set of $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \ge 2$ and the energy density $F(x,ξ)$ satisfies nearly linear growth conditions with respect to the gradient variable. The main novelty of this work lies in the identification of a suitable quantitative balance between the logarithmic degeneration of the ellipticity and an Orlicz-Sobolev regularity of the partial map $x\to {F(x,ξ)}$ that is sufficient to obtain the Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers.

candidates.title: Exponential decay of the quasilinear Maxwell system caused by conductivity on a collar
candidates.abstract: We study the anisotropic, quasilinear Maxwell system on a bounded domain $Ω$ with perfectly conducting boundary conditions. It is damped via a conductivity $σ$ which is strictly positive on its support containing a collar of the boundary. We prove that solutions exist globally and decay exponentially to $0$ if there are no magnetic charges on $Ω$, no electric charges off the support of $σ$, and the initial fields are small. Our approach relies on a splitting of the solution via adapted Helmholtz decompositions and an observability-type estimate for a related system without charges, shown by means of Morawetz multipliers. Moreover, one has to control the space derivatives of the solution by its time derivatives, exploiting the structure of the system. The discontinuity of $σ$ introduces an interface which poses significant challenges in all these steps, besides those coming from the quasilinear terms.

candidates.title: Large deviations and conditional laws for a time-integrated logarithm of averaged Gaussian squares
candidates.abstract: Systems with identical instantaneous power distributions can have very different probabilities of insufficient service over a fixed interval. We study the lower tail of the time-integrated logarithm of a weighted mean of $d$ independent squared Gaussian paths as $d\to\infty$. A global entropy inequality resolves the nonconvex service constraint, identifies the unique Gaussian minimizer and controls the nonlinear likelihood weight far from that minimizer. Combined with a joint local limit, it yields sharp probabilities at fixed internal thresholds and conditional path laws: a Fredholm determinant enters the leading factor, and tangential Gaussian fluctuations are independent of the exponential service deficit. The approximations extend through moderate deviations to the central scale. For stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck paths, cancellation in the radial likelihood expansion yields relative error $O(d^{-1})$ on compact positive parameter families with proportions and saddles separated from zero. Genuine temporal covariance attenuation by correlation kernels for a type of positive limiting proportion increases the lower-tail rate, yet the finite-sample outage distributions cross near t

candidates.title: Approximation of the Nonautonomous Maxwell System with an Interface
candidates.abstract: To obtain higher-regularity solutions for nonautonomous Maxwell systems with an interface, we approximate the initial data and coefficients by smoother counterparts. To preserve compatibility conditions of the approximations, required to obtain solutions to the Maxwell systems, we systematically adjust the approximating sequence of initial data. While the existing well-posedness theory in [14] guarantees more regular solutions, standard a-priori estimates fail to ensure convergence in the desired norm. We overcome this by a mollification argument and a div-curl estimate from [4] and [7].

candidates.title: A Class of Coupled Forward-Backward Systems Under General Filtrations
candidates.abstract: We consider a class of coupled-forward backward systems defined on a general probability space assumed only to satisfy the usual conditions. We obtain existence and uniqueness results for arbitrary finite time horizons.

candidates.title: Coerciveness for complex Hessian type equations
candidates.abstract: We study complex Hessian type equations associated with right-Noetherian polynomials on compact Kähler manifolds of complex dimension $n$. For two such polynomials of the same degree $2\le d\le n$ in strict proper position, we prove that under the integrability condition and the assumption that the admissible space $\mathcal{H}_2$ is non-empty, smooth admissible solvability for $f_1$, the $d_1$-coerciveness of the associated variational functional $J_1$ on normalized potentials, and the numerical criterion for $f_1$ are equivalent to each other. This extends the existence-coerciveness correspondence of Chen-Ghosh-Wang to the lower-degree setting under weaker polynomial conditions.

candidates.title: On the Laugesen--Siudeja Conjecture: A Sharp Lower Bound and Failure of the Upper Bound
candidates.abstract: We prove the sharp lower bound in the Laugesen--Siudeja conjecture and give a counterexample to its upper bound. For every bounded convex planar domain, the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $λ_1$, the area $A$, and the centroidal polar moment of inertia $I$ satisfy $λ_1A^3/I>9π^2/2$. The constant is approached by thin isosceles triangles. The lower bound follows from a rectangle comparison in the principal directions of the covariance matrix and a planar random-triangle inequality. For the upper bound, we exhibit an isosceles trapezoid on which $λ_1A^3/I>12π^2$, using Temple's inequality and exact arithmetic.

candidates.title: Nonlinear stability of periodic waves in the Benjamin-Ono equation
candidates.abstract: We construct the Lyapunov functional for the periodic waves of the Benjamin-Ono equation based on the conservation of momentum, energy, and a higher-order energy, which exists due to integrability. Positivity of the second variation of the Lyapunov functional for perturbations in Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ is established by utilizing the basis properties of eigenfunctions of the linearized Benjamin-Ono equation in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. Coercivity of the Lyapunov functional for co-periodic and multiple-periodic perturbations yields the nonlinear orbital stability of the periodic waves in the periodic domain.

candidates.title: Freedom is all you need
candidates.comment: 26 pages. This manuscript was developed, produced, and edited entirely by humans
candidates.abstract: The functional calculus allows for the rigorous analysis of functions of matrices or even operators. The free functional calculus gives the natural class of functions over any category. We initiate the representation theory for taking a generic free functional calculus to the classical nc functional calculus going back to Taylor, Voiculescu and many others, with an eye towards learning of categories. The functional calculus on direct sum closed and locally similarity (i.e. change of coordinates) invariant domains inherits the niceties of complex analysis and large-scale parallel networks, such as automatic analyticity, free universal monodromy, which gives a hypothetical explanation for beneficial overfitting.

candidates.title: One exponential or two? Invertibility tests for Jordan epimorphisms
candidates.abstract: How many exponential factors must one test to recognise a Jordan epimorphism? Let \(T\colon A\to B\) be a unital linear surjection between complex Banach algebras, with \(B\) semisimple. Using a spectral-isometry theorem of Aznay and Chabbabi, we show that it suffices for \(T\) to send every product of two exponentials to an invertible element to force $T$ to be Jordan. If only single exponentials are tested, \(T\) is a Jordan epimorphism if and only if its kernel is a two-sided ideal, or equivalently a left ideal. A resolvent estimate on a logarithmic spiral shows that a single exponential suffices when the source is a \(C^*\)-algebra or the group algebra \(\ell^1(G)\) of a discrete group. A separate argument, which does not use the spectral-isometry theorem, shows that a single exponential also suffices when the target is a \(C^*\)-algebra with a faithful family of tracial states.

candidates.title: Energy-preserving Bayesian model reduction: closed-form structured posteriors and probabilistic stability certificates for quadratic operator inference
candidates.abstract: Bayesian operator inference learns reduced-order models (ROMs) with polynomial structure from state data and returns a closed-form Gaussian posterior over the reduced operators. That posterior is unconstrained, so it gives positive probability to operators with unbounded dynamics, and current practice controls this only through finite-horizon simulation tests on a few samples. We show that energy preservation of the quadratic operator is a set of linear equality constraints, which can be imposed exactly inside the Bayesian formulation without losing the closed form. In particular, the constrained posterior follows from one Kalman-type update of the unconstrained one, and its samples are obtained exactly, by the same correction applied to unconstrained draws. Under this structure, global boundedness for all initial conditions and bounded inputs reduces to a linear matrix condition on the symmetric part of the linear operator. The simulation test is then replaced by a probabilistic stability certificate: the posterior probability that the ROM is globally bounded, estimated with exact confidence bounds; the posterior restricted to certified models is then sampled exactly by rejection.

candidates.title: Disk 2-point functions for conformal loop ensemble: a derivation from the SLE loop CFT
candidates.comment: 27 pages, 2 figures. This paper is aimed at theoretical physicists. In particular, not all arguments are mathematically rigorous
candidates.abstract: We give a derivation of the bulk two-point functions of two-dimensional critical loop models in the disk based on conformal loop ensembles (CLE) and the conformal field theory of SLE loop measures developed by Baverez--Jego. Combining local Ward identities with the spectral resolution of the SLE-loop CFT, we express the two-point functions as contour integrals involving known CLE three-point structure constants and Virasoro conformal blocks. With a suitable choice of contour, these integrals are absolutely convergent and provide a unified representation of a broad class of correlation functions, valid for both irrational and rational central charges. For irrational central charges, evaluating these integrals by residues determines the discrete closed-channel spectrum and yields expansions that agree with the analytic bootstrap predictions of Downing--Jacobsen--Nivesvivat--Ribault--Saleur.

candidates.title: Pairing and modular: Generalized electrons and quasiholes inside the $\boxtimes$ of topological orders
candidates.abstract: We study the relationship between the pair creation mechanism in physics and the pairing ($\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}$) in mathematics, focusing on the modular and algebraic properties. We provide a way to couple two topologically ordered systems, $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{A'}$ sharing the common (non-group-like) structure $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}=\overline{\mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}}$, through the nonabelian anyon analog of the pair creation mechanism denoted as $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}=\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}\boxtimes \mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}$. We identify $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the generalized version of electron operators in general topological orders or hidden current with (half-)integer spin involving the conformal embeddings. We provide a way to construct $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the hidden topological operator and identify $\mathbf{A}\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}\mathbf{A'}$, a general class of topoloical orders, as the $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$-extended symmetry topological field theory. We also conjecture a series of underlying (unexplored) modular invariants, connecting the conformal embedding and the pairing.

candidates.title: Rigidity in the Lichnerowicz inequality for word-length semigroups
candidates.abstract: We give an operator-algebraic characterization of Cayley graphs that are partial cubes, that is, embed isometrically into a hypercube. More precisely, noncommutative versions of the Lichnerowicz inequality control the spectral gap of the generator of a quantum Markov semigroup by the constant in the complete $Γ_2$-criterion of Junge and Zeng or the constant in the geometric Ricci criterion of Junge, LaRacuente and Li. We show that for word-length semigroups on group von Neumann algebras, equality in either of these inequalities occurs exactly when the Cayley graph is a partial cube.

candidates.title: Algebraic dark solitons versus rogue waves in the massive Thirring model
candidates.abstract: We address the existence of algebraically decaying solitary waves on the nonzero wave background in the massive Thirring model (MTM) in laboratory coordinates. We find the precise condition of the spectral stability and instability of the nonzero wave background. In the case of instability, we distinguish modulational, side-band, and full-band instabilities and show that the rogue wave exists if and only if the nonzero wave background is modulationally unstable. For the other unstable cases and in the case of stability, we show that there exist exactly two algebraic dark solitons which correspond to the end points in the admissible range of the wave speed for the dark soliton propagation.

candidates.title: Semi-regular admixed arrays: asymptotic enumeration and when information is additive
candidates.abstract: In genomic data analysis, admixed arrays are pairs of matrices recording the local ancestry and the allele at each position of the haplotypes of admixed individuals. We study two-way diploid admixed arrays with $N$ individuals and $P$ loci under two families of constraints: local ancestry tallies, which fix the number of ancestry assignments per individual, and ancestry-specific sums, which fix the allele count per locus and ancestry. These two constraint families correspond to summaries of admixed genetic data investigated in biomedical and genomic applications. In the semi-regular regime, where all tallies and sums are uniform, we use complex martingale techniques to derive asymptotic formulas for the number of doubly constrained arrays as $N$ and $P$ grow with bounded ratio, over the whole feasible region. The leading term is governed by the Shannon entropy of the frequencies of the four possible pairs of entries at a position of the two matrices; on the boundary one or two of them vanish, changing the Gaussian correction. We then ask whether the two families carry information additively, that is, whether an independence heuristic predicts the doubly constrained count up to a bo

candidates.title: Convergence of a finite element Chorin projection method for the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations
candidates.abstract: We analyze a fully discrete finite element projection method for the stochastic incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and multiplicative noise. We show solvability and uniform moment estimates for the intermediate and the corrected velocity approximations under the assumption that the initial data is square-integrable and divergence free, and that the deterministic forcing term is bounded in $L^{q}(0,T;H^{-1}(D))$ for a sufficiently large $q$. Under standard stability and approximation assumptions on the finite element spaces and a coupling condition on the spatial and temporal discretization parameters, we prove convergence of a subsequence to a martingale solution of the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations. The analysis combines the complementary spatial and temporal estimates of the predicted and the corrected velocity approximations and uses the numerical dissipation to identify their common limit. We establish tightness of the piecewise constant temporal interpolations of the velocity field approximations using Aldous' criterion combined with the uniform discrete moment estimates. The convergence result holds in two and three sp

candidates.title: Recognizing $k$-inducible Digraphs is NP-complete
candidates.abstract: A digraph is k-inducible if its arcs correspond to the pairwise majority relation of a preference profile with k voters. By McGarvey's theorem, every asymmetric digraph is k-inducible for some k, but for every fixed k there are digraphs that are not k-inducible. Whether a digraph is 1-inducible or 2-inducible can easily be decided in polynomial time. The complexity of deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible for every fixed $k\geq 3$ has been a long-standing open problem. We prove that deciding whether a tournament is 3-inducible is NP-complete and then leverage this result to show that deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible is NP-complete for every fixed $k\geq 3$. Our results imply that, unless P=NP, k-inducible digraphs cannot be characterized by finitely many forbidden induced subdigraphs.

candidates.title: Minkowski Correlation Functions (MCF): Long-range, robust shape descriptors for point patterns
candidates.abstract: A morphometric analysis of point patterns using Minkowski functionals is short-sighted, whereas correlation functions do not provide robust, i.e., additive shape descriptors. To combine the advantages of both standard techniques and to overcome their weaknesses, we introduce ring-based Minkowski correlation functions (MCFs) as robust and sensitive descriptors of disordered point patterns. By assigning to each point a spherical shell and quantifying the resulting two-phase morphology via Minkowski functionals, MCFs capture structural information across multiple length scales, remain sensitive at radii where conventional disk-based Minkowski functionals have saturated, and implicitly encode higher-order correlations beyond the pair correlation and structure factor. We present an exact and efficient algorithm for planar patterns extending the established disk-based morphological approach to long ranges. Applications across scales -- active colloids (Quincke rollers), longleaf pine trees, and the Hubble Ultra Deep Field -- demonstrate clear and systematic deviations from homogeneous Poisson references, with distinct responses of covered area, boundary length, and Euler characteristic.

candidates.title: The Power of Sampling for Finding Far-Apart Bases in Matroids
candidates.abstract: We study the geometry of matroids via the \emph{diameter} and \emph{dispersion} of the metric space of their bases. Given a matroid $M$, we ask if the diameter of its basis-exchange graph $\mathcal{G}(M)$ can be approximated by sampling two uniformly random bases. As our main result, we show that their expected distance is always at least $1/16$ of the diameter of $\mathcal{G}(M)$. While this might appear to follow from the edge-expansion properties established by Anari, Liu, Gharan and Vinzant (STOC'19), we show that this inutition is false by constructing a graph $G$ with edge-expansion at least $1$ for which sampling two random vertices does \emph{not} give a constant-factor approximation to its diameter. We turn to finding $k\geq 2$ maximally-diverse bases of a matroid, the $k$ (max--min) diversity problem. When $k=2$, the problem is solvable via matroid intersection. However, for $k\geq 3$ no polynomial-time approximation or hardness is known, even for diverse spanning trees. We show that sampling $k\geq 3$ bases provides a tight $Θ(\log k)$ approximation. We then combine structural insights about the local density of $\mathcal{G}(M)$ with classical LP-rounding techniques to o

candidates.title: The moments and asymptotic spectral distribution of the Grassmannian ensemble
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we study random density matrices constructed by taking partial traces of projections onto random subspaces of a bipartite Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B}$ distributed according to the pushforward measure of the action of the unitary group on the Grassmannian $\text{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B})$. This ensemble models a `typical' quantum subspace. All tracial moments of the density operator, as well as mixed tracial moments of reduced density operators, are computed explicitly using Weingarten calculus. There are several consequences of these results. In particular, we prove that the empirical spectral distribution of the density operator converges almost surely to a rescaled Marchenko-Pastur law. We also prove that this ensemble can be written as a sum of asymptotically free random density operators, leading to an alternative proof of the convergence of the spectral distribution. Finally, we compute the asymptotic expansion of the average entanglement entropy.

candidates.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning of Latent Patient Representations from Multi-Institutional EHRs
candidates.comment: 10 pages of main text (76 pages including references and appendices). Accepted for presentation at NeurIPS 2026
candidates.abstract: Electronic health records (EHRs) contain rich health information for uncovering latent patient representations and clinically meaningful subgroups. Learning from EHR data across institutions is valuable because representations learned at a single site may reflect local data patterns and lack generalizability, yet pooling patient-level records across institutions is often impractical because of privacy constraints and communication costs. We propose a communication-efficient, non-iterative federated spectral method for learning shared latent representation components from multi-institutional EHRs, in which each institution shares aggregate marginal frequencies and a low-rank spectral summary while keeping patient-level records local. A central server aggregates these summaries with the pooled marginal frequencies to recover both the shared low-rank structure and the canonical row-normalization direction required for interpretable representation recovery. We prove row-wise recovery guarantees and error bounds, with a leading federated variance term matching a corresponding lower bound under explicit regularity conditions. Simulations show that our method closely matches pooled analys

candidates.title: Critical Ising and Temperley-Lieb-Jones States: Cone Haag Duality and the Trivial Algebra Object
candidates.abstract: We compute the algebra object of two critical Ising states in the operator algebraic framework of fusion category symmetry. The boundary subalgebra is the even part of the Pauli chain, and its DHR category is the toric code. We treat two models. The first is the classical Ising model in two dimensions, through its row transfer matrix. The second is the Ising chain in a transverse field. For the critical transfer matrix state and for the ground state of the critical chain, the algebra object is exactly the tensor unit. In a second part we treat the critical Temperley--Lieb--Jones chains at $δ=2\cos(π/(k+2))$. For every $k\ge2$ the ground state selected by the vacuum block is pure and has trivial algebra object in the Drinfeld centre of the even part. At $k=2$ this recovers the critical Ising chain.

candidates.title: On the chromatic splitting conjecture in coheight $1$
candidates.abstract: This article confirms predictions made by Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture in stable homotopy theory. A consequence of our main theorem is that a certain map of $K(h-1)$-local $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-rings $\mathbb{S}_{K(h-1)}^{B\mathbb{Z}}\to L_{K(h-1)}\mathbb{S}_{K(h)}$ admits a retract, so long as $p-1$ does not divide $h-1$. If $h=2$ and $p$ is odd, we show this map is an isomorphism. We use methods from the theory of $p$-divisible groups and $p$-adic geometry. Along the way we prove an entirely new kind of "two-tower isomorphism," in analogy with Faltings' isomorphism between the Lubin--Tate and Drinfeld towers, which parametrizes $p$-divisible groups over characteristic $p$ perfectoid spaces with fixed generic fiber in terms of negative Banach--Colmez spaces. Using the two-tower isomorphism, we gain control over the continuous cohomology of the Morava stabilizer group $\mathbb{G}_h$ with coefficients in $π_*L_{K(h-1)}E_h$. To study the continuous action of $\mathbb{G}_h$ on $L_{K(h-1)} E_h$, it was necessary to develop the theory of solid Lubin--Tate spectra. Adapting Lurie's constructions, we attach a solid Lubin--Tate spectrum to $p$-divisible groups over a broad class o

candidates.title: Brane Tilings and Polygons with Two Interior Points
candidates.abstract: We fully classify the brane tilings and the 4d N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theories corresponding to toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds whose toric diagrams are convex lattice polygons with two interior lattice points. There are 45 such polygons up to GL(2,Z) transformations and lattice translations: 5 triangles, 19 quadrilaterals, 16 pentagons and 5 hexagons. We identify all 323 toric phases corresponding to these toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. For every toric phase, we present the brane tiling with its quiver and superpotential, the perfect matching matrix and the F- and D-term charge matrices. For each brane tiling, we study the mesonic moduli space of the corresponding abelian 4d N=1 theory through its Hilbert series and plethystic logarithm, and identify its generators and their leading relations. We also identify the mesonic global symmetry for each brane tiling and determine the superconformal U(1)R charges.

candidates.title: Tackling Many-Body Coulomb Singularity by Randomization
candidates.abstract: Many-body Coulomb dynamics is central to quantum chemistry and molecular simulation, yet the Coulomb singularity undermines both the standard error analysis and performance of product formulas. Even for the simple hydrogen ground state, the celebrated Trotter formulas converge more slowly than their nominal order, and going to higher order does not help. Randomization by itself does not resolve this. We show that conventional qDRIFT suffers the same loss of accuracy, and that for general initial states, the errors of both Trotter formulas and qDRIFT can decrease more slowly than any power of the number of time steps (logarithmically). To overcome these limitations, we introduce supersmoothing qDRIFT, a randomized product formula that turns a physical property of free particle propagation into an algorithmic resource. Our algorithm achieves an error bound that decreases linearly with the time step, uniformly over \textit{all} initial states and without any smoothness or energy assumptions. Combined with spatial discretization analysis, the resulting end-to-end gate count improves on those of qubitization and high-order Trotter formulas applied directly to the discretized Hamiltonian

candidates.title: Longest run for $q$-binary trials
candidates.abstract: We investigate the longest-run distribution for binary trials in which the success probability varies geometrically. Exact formulae are derived for the probability mass function and the cumulative distribution function of the length of the longest success run in a sequence of $q$-binary trials, using enumerative combinatorics. The setting covers independent but not necessarily identically distributed zero--one trials whose success probabilities follow a geometric rule, and the classical independent and identically distributed Bernoulli longest-run distribution is recovered in the limit $q\to 1$. A simulation study confirms accurate maximum likelihood estimation of the base success probability and the geometric parameter $q$, a well-calibrated and powerful boundary-corrected likelihood ratio test of the hypothesis that $q=1$, and close agreement between the analytical cumulative distribution function and its empirical counterpart.

candidates.title: $L^1$ stability of the entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$ without moment assumptions
candidates.abstract: We establish qualitative stability in $L^1$ and Ruzsa distance for Shannon's entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$, without any moment assumptions. The proof uses the optimal transport argument by Rioul (2017), majorization bounds of density rearrangements, and the stability of the sharp form of Young's inequality due to Christ (2019). Along the way we also extend recent one-dimensional results on de Bruijn's identity, the continuity of differential entropy, and the equality case of the entropy power inequality to random vectors of any dimension.

candidates.title: Penalty-Free Constrained Optimization on Dynamic Quantum Circuits via Phase-Protected Tunneling and Closed-Loop Spectral Ratchets
candidates.abstract: Embedding hard operational constraints into an unconstrained Hamiltonian via large penalty multipliers induces quadratic spectral aliasing during phase estimation and increases two-qubit gate depth. This paper proposes a penalty-free, closed-loop dynamic quantum circuit scheme, designated as Zeno-decoupled gauge-ratchet optimization (Z-GRO), for constrained binary optimization without outer-loop training. Reversible feasibility phase operators within symmetric dynamical-decoupling echoes confine evolution to the feasible subspace, while an interaction-correlated commutator gauge operator resolves initial symmetry stall. Directional cooling couples the unpenalized objective Hamiltonian to a reusable ancilla with a zero-two-qubit-gate threshold offset, bypassing echoed tunneling gates on retained branches. A survival-filtered Ramsey controller advances the threshold from a linear-programming bound with automatic overshoot rollback. Exact density-matrix and trajectory simulations on spin-glass and quadratic knapsack ensembles show a single-check discrimination gain above four orders of magnitude, improving ground-state probability by factors of 3.0 to 4.3 over quantum Zeno dynamics an

candidates.title: Convex Structure-Preserving EDMD: Passive Koopman Matrices as $Q$-Contractions
candidates.abstract: Extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) approximates the Koopman operator using a matrix based on a finite set of observables. However, the least-squares matrix of a port-Hamiltonian (pH) system is generally neither passive nor invariant-preserving. We demonstrate that the implicit midpoint discretization of a lifted pH model precisely preserves energy balance, passivity, and all linear Casimirs for every step size. For a fixed storage metric $Q$, the resulting Koopman matrices are the Cayley transforms of $(J-R)Q$, where $J$ is skew-symmetric and $R$ is positive semidefinite. This set does not depend on the step size and is the closure of all Q-contractions. This set is LMI-representable; therefore, structure-preserving EDMD, including ports through a discrete-time Kalman-Yakubovich-Popov condition and Casimirs through affine constraints, is a semidefinite program. The constrained estimate is a projection of the unconstrained estimate in the data-weighted norm and cannot increase estimation error when the population target is pH-compatible. For every $Q$-contraction, a certified bound on the lifted prediction error grows linearly at most in time, whereas it grows geometrically

candidates.title: Full-chip constrained quantum annealing via self-calibrating spin-susceptibility control
candidates.abstract: Discrete optimization in finance, power grids, and logistics requires minimizing Ising Hamiltonians under coupled linear constraints. However, quadratic-penalty formulations generate dense cliques that exhaust the minor-embedding capacity of sparse superconducting processors at 128-176 spins, and first-order dual subgradient schemes diverge or stall under constraint coupling. Accordingly, this study proposes a closed-loop primal-dual scheme, designated as Self-Calibrating Quantum Susceptibility Quasi-Newton (SelfCal-QSQN), in which linear constraints are encoded in longitudinal fields and dual curvature is reconstructed from single-shot spin-fluctuation covariances. This scheme requires no penalty couplers, slack qubits, or perturbation queries. Evaluated over 891 runs on D-Wave Advantage (5,612 qubits) and Advantage2 (4,560 qubits), SelfCal-QSQN achieves 83.3% full-chip exact feasibility, reduces high-constraint error by 6.1-20.1-fold over $K$-scaled first-order updates (138.4-323.3-fold over fixed-gain curvature), outperforms time-matched mixed-integer programming at 256 spins, and attains 95.0%-96.7% feasibility on non-native and inequality benchmarks. Moreover, the scheme is ro

candidates.title: Can pretrained Transformers deliver semiparametrically efficient inference?
candidates.abstract: Semiparametric models provide a broad framework for statistical inference, yet efficient estimation typically relies on influence function correction tailored to each estimand and on nuisance estimation repeated for every sample. We show that a single pretrained Transformer can deliver efficient estimation and valid inference for a family of estimands in one forward pass, without deriving efficient influence functions or estimating nuisance functions. Pretrained on simulated data with the true parameter as the only label, the Transformer learns the posterior mean and covariance of the queried estimand and hence returns an estimate and a Wald-type confidence region. Theoretically, we prove that, for locally flat pretraining priors of slowly growing complexity, the posterior mean is efficient for every queried estimand. The Transformer inherits this efficiency with asymptotically exact coverage, in probability over evaluation populations and queries, even under distribution shift. We also reveal that the guarantee places much higher demands on pretraining when the data-generating distribution is fixed, as in classical frequentist inference. candidates.title: Additive cubes are avoidable by a non-uniform morphism of length $6$ over $\{0,a,b\}$ (with $b \ge 4$ and $\gcd(a,b) = 1$)
candidates.abstract: We prove that additive cubes are avoidable over every ternary alphabet $\{0, a, b\}$ with $1 \le a < b$, $\gcd(a, b) = 1$, and $b \ge 4$, thereby solving and extending Rao's~(2015) conjecture from $b \ge 6$ down to $b \ge 4$. Our construction applies a single dual pair of parameterized non-uniform morphisms of image length at most~$6$ to the additive-cube-free word $\mathbf{w}$ of Cassaigne et al.~(2014). For $b \ge 10$, we prove that every additive square in the image is an abelian square, reducing additive cubes to abelian cubes; the absence of abelian cubes and the $24$ finite cases with $4 \le b \le 9$ are then certified via the finite-graph method of Jamet and Rosenfeld~(2026).

candidates.title: Bridging Badiou's Gaps: Topos Theory and the Bodies of Mathematical Expression
candidates.abstract: This article develops a second stage of an argument begun in 2013, revisiting Alain Badiou's use of topos theory in Being and Event and Logics of Worlds. The previous article diagnosed Badiou's reduction of topos theory to its atomistic, localic form as the scientific scapegoat in his attack on 'democratic materialism'. Now I ask what follows when this logicist illusion is dispelled and the categorical alternative is taken seriously, particularly with respect to forcing, semantic expression, and mathematical subjectification that constitute the key elements of Badiou's earlier work. I thus reconstruct Badiou's own arguments in a corrected form, while transferring them to a categorical framework. The aim is not to introduce new mathematical results, but to identify what is conceptually lost through their reduction to set-theoretic formalism. In particular, I describe Cohen's forcing argument in the context of Grothendieck topoi and Kripke-Joyal semantics, thereby explicating the geometric structures implicit in Badiou's thinking. This reconstruction further brings into view a different way of understanding Badiou's concepts of subject, body, and change. Rather than treating a topos

candidates.title: Error-Corrected Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Optimal Control of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles under Uncertainty
candidates.abstract: We solve open-loop optimal control problems under parametric uncertainty using a physics-informed DeepONet that returns trajectories for all sampled scenarios in one evaluation. Trained only on the residual at generic controls, the operator is reused across targets and horizons. Because a gradient-based optimizer exploits surrogate errors, we correct the prediction by one Newton step on the dynamics, computed for all scenarios and times by one parallel scan. The corrected state has a second-order error bounded by the residual alone, and the corrected cost is honest for every control up to the sampling error. On a fixed-wing UAV benchmark, the corrected operator matches the accuracy of a batched Adam solver and an Ipopt solver at equal sample size and is 8 times faster than the Adam solver on the same GPU at a few hundred scenarios and 15 times faster than Ipopt on a CPU.

candidates.title: Stinespring's Dilation, Universal-NOT, and Limitations of Quantum Uncoupled Learning
candidates.abstract: Uncoupled learning, in which players know only their own payoff, are a standard model of decentralized learning toward Nash equilibrium. We study their quantum counterpart, where strategies are quantum states and, in each round, a player receives a physical copy of their opponent's current strategy and updates their own state by a quantum channel. This adds to uncoupledness a constraint with no classical analogue: every update must be physically realizable. In fact, this constraint is decisive in conjugation games, in which Bob has a strictly dominant pure strategy and Alice's unique best response is its transpose. In this work, we show some limitations of uncoupled (learning) dynamics in finding the Nash equilibrium for conjugation games. First, we prove that no autonomous, memoryless, uncoupled dynamics converge to Nash equilibrium in a family of four single-qubit conjugation games. Specifically, any memoryless channel that keeps all four equilibria fixed will leave Alice's strategy frozen. This result also extends to $4^n$ games on $n$-qubit registers. Second, we show that this barrier disappears with a small classical memory: for any finite family of $L$ pure targets, a guess-a

candidates.title: Sparse Analytic Representation of Stationary Processes with Bounded Spectral Density
candidates.abstract: We consider centered second-order stationary processes Y={Y_t}{t\in R} with bounded spectral density S_Y and develop a sparse analytic representation framework. A nontrivial stationary process on the real line generally does not belong to L^2(Ω,L^2(R)), since stationarity implies E||Y||{L^2(R)}^2=\infty. To overcome this infinite-energy obstruction, we replace the sample-path viewpoint by the bounded linear operator \widetilde Y: L^2(R) \to L^2(Ω), with \widetilde Y(f) = \int_{R} \hat{f}(ξ) Z_Y(dξ), where Z_Y is the orthogonal random measure in the spectral representation of Y. Applying \widetilde Y to Cauchy kernels in the upper and lower half-planes yields random analytic functions U_+ and U_-. For α>1, we prove U_+ \in L^2(Ω, B_α^2(C^+)) and U_- \in L^2(Ω, B_α^2(C^-)), where B_α^2(C^\pm) are weighted Bergman spaces. We combine U_+ and U_- into U(ω,z) = U_+ for z \in C^+, and U_- for z \in C^-, and with B_α= B_α^2(C^+) \oplus B_α^2(C^-), prove U \in L^2(Ω, B_α). We establish boundary vanishing, energy identity, and convergence, and derive covariance identities for the coefficients. candidates.title: Idempotent generically stable measures in NIP groups
candidates.abstract: Let $μ$ be a global generically stable Keisler measure on a type-definable group in an NIP theory. Then $μ$ is idempotent if and only if it is the unique translation-invariant measure on its type-definable stabilizer subgroup. This resolves the NIP case of the Idempotent Measure problem studied by Chernikov, Gannon, and Krupiński.

candidates.title: Integral Multipliers and Arithmetic Obstructions for Two-Hidden-Layer ReLU Maxima
candidates.abstract: We study exact representations of maximum functions by ReLU networks with two hidden layers and integer parameters. The least positive output multiplier is two for the six-input maximum, and either two or six for the seven-input maximum. We obtain these bounds from integral cubical fillings and a coefficient-preserving passage from polytope identities to networks. For the coordinate-facet complex of the six-simplex, we compute a coning index of six over the integers and three after inverting two, allowing arbitrary integral directions within each facet. A class in the homology of the unrestricted kernel complex characterizes the remaining seven-input problem; its vanishing is equivalent to an integral filling of a fixed target. We also construct a finite character that separates rational from three-local representability in a dictionary containing two known constructions and all pairs of edge-disjoint three-edge forests. This obstruction permits nonsymmetric coefficients and is confined to the specified dictionary. Control of lower-dimensional remainders yields a sufficient criterion in the top-dimensional quotient. candidates.title: Moonshine Conjecture Formalized
candidates.comment: 7 pages, 0 figures. A case study in Lean formalization, semantic trust, and repository versioning
candidates.abstract: The celebrated and intimidating Moonshine Conjecture has now been formalized in Lean. This achievement might suggest that, once a sufficiently large library compiles, the principal mathematical work is complete. This paper tells a less optimistic story. During our formalization project, we repeatedly encountered two problems that a formally checked proof alone does not settle: (1) whether the formal statements actually express the mathematics we humans expect, and (2) how that meaning survives as the repositories and their dependencies evolve. We argue that there is no magic pill that turns a large agent-produced library into mathematics a community can trust. Even after the proofs are checked by the Lean kernel, someone must judge whether the definitions and statements express the intended mathematics and whether future updates preserve that meaning. This work, even when done, can only be trusted. We must therefore return to the usual trust model: relying on the mathematical judgment of maintainers and expert communities. But semantic review is expensive, making it tempting to keep producing code and take successful kernel checks as sufficient grounds for trust. This shortcut accu

candidates.title: Subspace Inference for Multilayer Latent Space Networks: Intrinsic Geometry and One-Step Estimator
candidates.abstract: Multilayer networks on a common node set, such as brain connectomes of several animals with one layer per animal, often share a low-dimensional geometry but differ in how strongly each layer expresses it and in node activity. We study a multilayer latent space network model that combines an invariant subspace common to all layers with layer-specific interaction matrices and node-by-layer degree effects. By introducing the generalized Cayley transform of the invariant subspace, we characterize the intrinsic geometry of the model and obtain sharp convergence rates for the maximum likelihood estimator, asymptotic normality and Neyman orthogonality for vertex-level parameters, and asymptotic normality for the interaction matrices with a non-negligible bias. Plug-in estimates of the bias and covariance give debiased confidence regions and tests of equality between layers. We also propose an easy-to-implement one-step estimator that attains the same vertex-level limits. In a real-world mouse connectome dataset, the inbred strain that lacks a corpus callosum shows about twice the hemispheric segregation of the other three strains.

candidates.title: Calabi-Yau at 50: mathematical discovery in the age of AI
candidates.comment: 27 pages. Based on invited talk at "Calabi-Yau at 50: The Legacy and Future", held at Tsinghua University in September, 2026
candidates.abstract: Using the golden jubilee of Yau's proof of the Calabi conjecture as a spring-board, we discuss how the dataset of Calabi-Yau manifolds brought together mathematicians and physicists since the 1980s, and then further brought in the world of machine-learning and AI since 2017. We give a historical account on the growth of the field of ``AI-assisted mathematics'' in the last decade, and comment on what culminated in 2026 as perhaps the most dramatic year in the history of mathematics since Euclid.

candidates.title: Spectral Estimation with Deformed Decompression
candidates.abstract: Sample covariance matrices are fundamental objects in machine learning and statistics, with valuable information encoded into their eigenvalues. When treating modern problems, the scale of these matrices can become prohibitive for tractable computation. This creates a critical need for "spectral decompression": a method for inferring the eigenspectrum of a very large-scale model using only information from its smaller realizations. Existing methods fall into two main categories: those relying on spectral inversion; and those that rely on Free Decompression techniques. On the one hand, spectral inversion is a fundamentally ill-posed problem that is notoriously unstable, often failing to yield reliable results in finite-size settings. On the other hand, while Free Decompression was recently proposed to address this scaling, its reliance on the Nica-Speicher framework restricts its use to unitarily invariant ensembles, a symmetry condition that subsampled covariance matrices fail to satisfy. In this work, we introduce Deformed Decompression (DD), a novel framework for the stable, forward-extrapolation of spectral densities. By leveraging properties of the companion matrix, DD recasts

candidates.title: Uncovering Multimorbidity Patterns Through a Novel Randomized Clustering Algorithm
candidates.abstract: Patients with several chronic conditions rarely share the same combination: in four years of the nationally representative Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS), we find 32,789 distinct combinations of two to seven conditions, and over 90% of those involving four or more occur in a single patient. Methods that search for common combinations discard most of this heterogeneity. We present the Randomized Length Sequential Clustering Algorithm (RLSCA), which links diseases by lift, a pairwise association measure counted only above a user-set support threshold. A mixed-integer program repeatedly selects and removes the group of conditions with the greatest internal lift, up to a random size; 100 iterations yield a database of clusters scored by size, rediscovery frequency, and body systems spanned. In MEPS 2019, stratified by age and sex, RLSCA recovers known groupings at a high threshold, such as diabetes with lipid disorders and hypertension, and at a lower threshold returns clusters of up to eight conditions spanning five body systems. candidates.title: Estimating contextual networks via Fisher-scoring surrogate likelihood
candidates.abstract: When networks are accompanied by vertex-level covariates, effectively integrating and aligning the information underlying both data sources becomes a natural yet critical task. Current spectral approaches, despite their popularity, may yield suboptimal results and necessitate the specification of additional tuning parameters that are contingent upon unobservable signal-to-noise ratios. We propose a tuning-free, likelihood-based learning framework for estimating latent positions in contextual generalized random dot product graphs in the presence of high-dimensional vertex covariates with a low-rank structure. Our method constructs a smooth surrogate likelihood and implements a Fisher-scoring algorithm to iteratively estimate latent positions without introducing additional tuning parameters that depend on the network sparsity. We establish the consistency and asymptotic normality of the Fisher-scoring estimator. Application to real-world data further demonstrates the method's practical utility, offering a principled and scalable alternative to spectral approaches for analyzing contextual networks in high-dimensional settings.

candidates.title: The regular $N$-gon maximizes first positive Neumann eigenvalue among simple polygons with at most $N$ sides and fixed area
candidates.abstract: Let $Φ(P)=|P|μ_1(P)$, where $μ_1(P)$ is the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of $P$. For every $N\ge3$, the regular $N$-gon $R_N$ uniquely maximizes $Φ$, up to congruence, among simple polygons of fixed area with at most $N$ sides. The values $Φ(R_N)$ increase strictly with $N$. The maximization theorem answers Laugesen's question \cite[Problem~(1), p.~405]{ABLW} and proves the polygonal Szegő--Weinberger conjecture of Laugesen and Siudeja \cite[Conjecture~6.36]{LSH}. It also implies that the triangular lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of the Voronoi cell at fixed covolume.

candidates.title: Littlestone Dimension and Its Dual
candidates.abstract: The dual Littlestone dimension of a concept class $\mathcal{H}\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal{X}}$, $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}):=\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H}^*)$, is the Littlestone dimension of the dual class $\mathcal{H}^*$, obtained by exchanging the roles of domain points and hypotheses. A classical result of Shelah implies that $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})$ and $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H})$ are finite simultaneously, and quantitative results of Hodges [Mathematika, 1981] imply the doubly exponential bound $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}))}}$. Malliaris and Moran [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2024] asked whether this bound is optimal. We answer this by proving the improved bound \[ \operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H})^2)}. \] An exponential dependence is necessary, as witnessed by the class of all binary hypotheses on a finite domain.

candidates.title: A proof of the polygonal Faber--Krahn inequality
candidates.abstract: We prove that, for every integer $n\ge3$, the regular $n$-gon uniquely minimizes the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, up to congruence, among simple polygons of prescribed area with at most $n$ sides. We also obtain the optimal linear correction when fewer than $n$ sides are present. The proof combines a partition into convex cells with a mixed boundary comparison. Among convex polygons of fixed area and fixed sum of base angles less than $π$, the isosceles triangle minimizes the first eigenvalue with Dirichlet conditions on the base and Neumann conditions elsewhere. A comparison of Fourier transforms of conformal area densities proves this inequality and the corresponding upper bounds for inverse spectral moments of integer order at least two. We prove strict log-convexity of an interpolation of the eigenvalues of regular polygons of unit area for real parameters at least four. We then derive sharp hexagonal bounds for periodic convex polygonal tilings and asymptotic bounds for convex polygonal partitions of a fixed convex polygon, with an explicit correction for boundary junctions.

candidates.title: Well-posedness and finite-time breakdown for Euler-alignment systems with diffusive chemotaxis
candidates.abstract: We investigate a recent class of pressureless Euler systems arising in biological contexts, in which the velocity evolution is driven, besides the nonlocal alignment interaction, by the gradient of a concentration self-produced by the population. We first establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, in a class requiring no spatial derivative of the initial population density, together with a continuation criterion. We then derive sufficient conditions on the initial data for finite-time breakdown in the multidimensional setting, with an explicit upper bound for the maximal time of existence. Numerical simulations complement the analysis and illustrate the transition between regular and singular regimes, and the role of the chemotactic strength in the onset of blow-up.

candidates.title: Intervals of limit points for $B_α$-spectral radii
candidates.abstract: For a finite simple graph $G$, let \[ B_α(G)=αA(G)+(1-α)L(G)=(1-α)D(G)+(2α-1)A(G),\qquad 0\leq α\leq 1. \] We study the limit points of the spectral radii of these matrices. Put $a_α=1-α$, $b_α=|2α-1|$, and $w_α=a_α+b_α$. All these points are realized by connected bipartite graphs of maximum degree at most $d$. We extend the induced-subgraph interpolation of Alon and Wei from $A$ to $aD+bA$, and obtain a unified proof using bipartite Ramanujan graphs. Consecutive intervals overlap for large $d$; hence the set of $B_α$-limit points contains a half-line for every $α\neq 1/2$. At $α=1/2$, one has $B_{1/2}=D/2$, and the set of spectral radii is discrete. Combining uniform edge subdivisions with generalized Bethe decorations, we improve the Laplacian and signless Laplacian half-line to $[29/5,\infty)$, verified by an exact rational certificate.
